purpose: How a gold-plating bench proves the deposit rather than asserting it: classing each piece by the wear duty it will actually see and turning that into a thickness and underlayer specification, writing acceptance criteria and worst-case measurement zones before any gold flows, running ride-along witness coupons so destructive evidence never costs a customer's ring, measuring thickness through named method classes (XRF, coulometric, microsection arbitration) with each method's calibration limits and error modes understood, testing adhesion with the ASTM B571-class battery chosen for the goods and reading crack against peel correctly, sampling batches on a plan fixed before the run, and recording every number against job, bath state and rack position so a thickness statement, a label class referral or a durability estimate can always be traced to the measurement and the method that produced it.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

commercial plating chemistry operated per the specific product's technical data sheet; this KB verifies the deposit that chemistry produced and never specifies bath setpoints, replenishment or corrections of its own

measurement in a small shop is a mix of in-house instruments and bought-in services: XRF may be a benchtop unit, a handheld or a per-sample service at a refiner or plating supplier, and coulometric testing is usually the first thickness instrument a shop owns

published standard families are used as method and class names only (XRF per the ISO 3497 / ASTM B568 class, coulometric per the ISO 2177 / ASTM B504 class, microsection per the ISO 1463 class, adhesion per the ASTM B571 class, sampling structured on the ISO 2859 class, thickness-claim ladders per the US FTC Jewelry Guides class and the ISO 27874 class); the exact edition, thresholds and applicability are verified in the current standard and in the selling jurisdiction, never recited from memory

the sibling gates exist and are separate: colour and appearance acceptance is judged elsewhere and defect root-cause and rework routing are decided elsewhere; this KB proves thickness and adhesion, refers everything else, and releases jointly rather than alone

every reagent and stripping electrolyte this KB touches sits under the same chemical-safety obligation classes as the plating room (segregation, storage, labeling, PPE, ventilation, training, emergency readiness) with the workplace and hazmat rules of the jurisdiction verified; cyanide-class solutions and acids are never mixed, never stored together and never share a drain
exclusions: karat-colour families, hue levers, master-panel comparison, defined-light evaluation and honest advice about achievable colour on a given stack - the sibling Colour & Appearance Control KB owns appearance; this KB proves the deposit and takes colour acceptance as a parallel gate it releases with

cause trees for peeling, blistering, pitting, burning, dull or hazy deposits, staining and uneven coverage, evidence-based root-cause assignment to prep, chemistry or process, and the strip-and-replate decision with its documented-approval and stripping-safety gates - the sibling Defect Diagnosis & Rework Routing KB; this KB detects and names an adhesion or thickness failure with its evidence and refers it there rather than diagnosing or reworking

performing surface preparation, racking, current-path design, bath analysis, dosing or contamination treatment - the prep, chemistry and process specialists own the tanks; this KB measures what came out and refers a failing result back to them

approving regulated label terms: 'gold flashed', 'gold plated', 'gold electroplate', 'heavy gold electroplate', 'vermeil', 'gold filled' and 'rolled gold plate' are compliance classes whose thresholds, base-metal conditions and marking rules belong to the selling jurisdiction - verify the current rules before any claim; this KB maps a measured number to the class it would have to satisfy, flags claim-shaped language, and never approves a label

guaranteed wear-life figures, warranty periods or durability promises invented as fact - every durability statement is either backed by a named measurement or given as an estimate that names its method and its band

accredited testing that only a laboratory can issue: nickel-release testing to the EN 1811 class with the EN 12472 wear-and-corrosion simulation, conformant salt-spray exposure to the ISO 9227 / ASTM B117 class, and fire-assay arbitration to the ISO 11426 class are send-out obligations this KB schedules and files, never simulates in-house
personalized legal, medical or financial advice - nickel sensitisation, chemical exposure and product-liability questions route to the applicable regulation classes and to qualified professionals

competency_questions.question: What is this verification gate actually responsible for proving, and what does it hand off to the colour gate and the defect gate instead of deciding itself?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VERIFICATION_CHARTER states the two claims this gate owns (thickness against a specification and adhesion of the deposit to its substrate), names the referral lines to appearance and to defect diagnosis, and states that it flags rather than approves regulated label wording

competency_questions.question: How thick does the gold on this particular piece need to be, and what decides that before anyone quotes a price?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WEAR_CLASS_SPECIFICATION derives the thickness class from the service duty of the piece (skin contact, abrasion, handling) as a mechanism, expresses bands as handbook-class guidance rather than invented guarantees, and ties the chosen class to gold cost and cycle time

competency_questions.question: What is the layer under the gold doing, and does it get specified and measured too?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: UNDERLAYER_SPEC explains the barrier, leveling and diffusion-blocking roles of the underlayer, states that it carries its own thickness specification and measurement, and routes nickel skin-contact questions to the regulation class rather than answering them

competency_questions.question: Where on the piece do I put the probe, and why is the average of a few readings not an answer?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WORST_CASE_ZONE_RULE names the low-current-density and high-wear zones as the acceptance points, explains why current distribution makes recesses and inside surfaces thinner than proud faces, and requires the zones to be marked before the run

competency_questions.question: What has to be written down before the first part enters the tank so that acceptance is not invented after the numbers come back?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA_PREWRITE lists the criteria fixed in advance (thickness class per zone, underlayer window, adhesion methods and their pass conditions, sample size, disposition rules) and states the rule that criteria written after results always pass

competency_questions.question: The tests I trust most are destructive and the goods belong to a customer - what do I destroy instead?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WITNESS_COUPON_DISCIPLINE requires coupons and offcuts of the same stack to ride the same rack in the same run, explains why separately-plated coupons do not represent the batch, and states which tests must be run on the witness rather than on the goods

competency_questions.question: When can I believe an XRF thickness number, and when is the instrument confidently lying to me?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: XRF_METHOD_CLASS gives the non-destructive method with its geometry, spot-size and thin-coating limits, and XRF_CALIBRATION_INTEGRITY makes stack-matched calibration standards a precondition for recording any number

competency_questions.question: What does a coulometric test give me that XRF does not, and what do I do when the two methods disagree?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COULOMETRIC_METHOD_CLASS describes the anodic-dissolution method, its per-layer electrolytes and its destructive spot, and METHOD_CROSS_CHECK gives the disagreement procedure ending in microsection-class arbitration or a mass-balance cross-check

competency_questions.question: How do I write a thickness number on a job ticket or say it to a customer without overclaiming?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MEASUREMENT_UNCERTAINTY_STATEMENT requires every number to travel with its method class, its measurement point, its calibration basis and a stated band, and forbids a bare figure presented as an exact property of the whole piece

competency_questions.question: Which adhesion tests apply to these particular goods, and which of them would wreck the piece if I ran it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ADHESION_TEST_SELECTION maps goods to an ASTM B571-class battery, and BEND_WRAP_TEST, TAPE_CROSSHATCH_TEST and THERMAL_QUENCH_TEST each state what they stress, what they miss and which goods they must never be run on

competency_questions.question: The bent witness shows fine lines under the loupe - is that a rejected batch or a normal result?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COHESIVE_VS_ADHESIVE_CALL separates cohesive microcracking of a hard deposit at a tight radius from adhesive lifting that exposes underlayer or substrate, requires magnified inspection and a photographed record, and makes only the adhesive case a reject

competency_questions.question: How many pieces out of this batch do I actually measure, and what forces me to requalify the whole product instead of just checking the batch?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SAMPLING_PLAN fixes first-article and per-batch sample size and rack-position spread before the run, and QUALIFICATION_VS_ROUTINE lists the changes (product, stack, chemistry, rack, instrument) that force a fresh qualification lot

competency_questions.question: Can this piece be called vermeil or gold plated on the tag, and who is allowed to sign off on that word?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LABEL_CLAIM_CLASS_MAP maps measured thickness and fineness onto the claim ladder as compliance classes with base-metal conditions, requires jurisdiction verification, and states that this gate flags rather than approves; ACCREDITED_SENDOUT_BOUNDARY names which evidence must come from an accredited laboratory before any claim leaves the shop

competency_questions.question: What can I honestly tell the customer about how long this finish will last, and what has to be on file before the parts go out the door?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DURABILITY_STATEMENT_HONESTY gives the measured-band-plus-method form of a wear statement and forbids invented wear-life guarantees, VERIFICATION_RECORD defines the traceable row and retained sample filed before stock movement, and RELEASE_DISPOSITION defines accept, hold, refer and reject with the joint-release rule

glossary.definition: The service duty a plated piece will actually see - decorative display, occasional wear, daily skin-contact wear, or high-abrasion wear such as a ring shank or a bracelet clasp - used to choose a thickness specification before any number is quoted. It is a mechanism, not a promise: heavier duty demands more deposit, and the achievable band for each class comes from handbook-class guidance, the chemistry supplier's data and the shop's own logged results, never from an invented figure.

The point on a piece where the deposit is thinnest and the wear is highest, typically a low-current-density recess, an inside ring surface, a chain link contact face or a shielded area behind a setting. Acceptance is judged there rather than on a proud, well-thrown outer face, because current distribution can leave a recess at a fraction of the thickness measured on the outside.

A flat coupon or wire offcut of the same substrate and layer stack as the work, hung on the same rack in the same run so it experiences the same bath state and current path. It is the sacrificial article for destructive evidence - coulometric spots, bend and wrap, thermal quench, cross-section - so no customer's piece is consumed to produce a number.

Non-destructive X-ray fluorescence thickness and composition measurement of the ISO 3497 / ASTM B568 class. It is fast and can be used on finished goods, but its answer depends on calibration standards matching the actual layer stack, on a measurement spot that fits inside a flat area, and on the coating being thick enough that the layer beneath does not dominate the signal.

Destructive spot thickness measurement of the ISO 2177 / ASTM B504 class: a gasketed cell anodically dissolves the coating at constant current and the endpoint appears as a potential change at the underlayer, with charge converted to thickness. It uses a proprietary electrolyte matched to each coating and substrate pair, leaves a small stripped spot, and is the affordable in-house anchor for thin deposits that XRF handles poorly.

Mounting, cutting, polishing and measuring a cross-section of the coating under a microscope, of the ISO 1463 class. It destroys the sample and takes real time and skill, which is why it is reserved for arbitration: when two other methods disagree beyond their stated bands, when a buyer disputes a number, or when a layer stack needs to be seen rather than inferred.

The set of adhesion methods of the ASTM B571 class - bend and wrap over a mandrel, cross-hatch and tape, thermal shock by heating and quenching, burnishing - chosen per goods rather than run wholesale. Each member stresses the coating-substrate interface differently, and a coating can pass a gentle member while failing a severe one, which is why the battery is selected in advance and its members are not treated as interchangeable.

Adhesive failure is the coating letting go of what is beneath it - lifting, flaking, peeling, exposing underlayer or base metal - and is a reject. Cohesive failure is the coating cracking within itself while staying bonded, which a hard cobalt- or nickel-hardened gold routinely does at a tight bend radius; under magnification cracks with no lifted edge are an expected characteristic of the deposit, not an adhesion reject.

The set of compliance classes that tie a marketing word to a measured minimum thickness, a minimum fineness and sometimes a required base metal - the US FTC Jewelry Guides class distinguishes flashed or washed from electroplate and heavy electroplate, vermeil additionally requires a sterling silver base, and gold filled or rolled gold plate describes mechanically clad stock that plating cannot produce at all. The ISO 27874 class covers gold and gold-alloy coatings for jewellery with its own thickness and fineness grades. Thresholds and wording rules are verified in the current standard and the selling jurisdiction before any claim.

A test that only an accredited laboratory can issue in a form that supports a claim to a buyer or a regulator - nickel release to the EN 1811 class with the EN 12472 wear-and-corrosion simulation for coated articles, conformant salt-spray exposure to the ISO 9227 / ASTM B117 class, fire assay to the ISO 11426 class. In-house equivalents are process-control screens only, and the certificate is filed against the product line rather than the batch.

nodes.definition: Fix, before any instrument is switched on, exactly what this gate is answerable for: that the deposit on a job meets a written thickness specification at the points that matter, and that it is genuinely bonded to what is underneath it. Everything else that a finished piece can be judged on has an owner elsewhere - whether the tone matches the customer's reference belongs to the appearance gate, why a blister formed belongs to defect diagnosis, and whether a tag may say vermeil belongs to whoever in the business signs compliance. The charter also fixes the two output forms this gate is allowed to emit: a measured statement that names its method, and a referral. It may never emit a promise. Writing this down first is what stops a bench from drifting into the habit of saying 'it looks thick enough' or 'that always holds' - the two sentences that create every later argument with a customer about a worn-through ring.

included: thickness proof against a written specification
adhesion proof of the deposit to its substrate
the referral lines to appearance, defect diagnosis and compliance
the allowed forms of an outgoing statement
excluded: colour and gloss acceptance
root-cause diagnosis and rework routing
approving a regulated label term
any tank-side chemistry or process adjustment

pros.claim: A written charter keeps the gate from absorbing questions it cannot answer, so referrals happen fast instead of being improvised at the counter
pros.example: a customer complaint about a dull ring is routed to the appearance gate on the same day instead of triggering an unnecessary thickness teardown

cons.claim: A narrow charter can feel obstructive when one person is the whole shop and would rather just answer everything
cons.example: a solo jeweller who is also the compliance signer still has to switch hats and record the decision under the compliance role, which feels like paperwork for its own sake

failure_modes: the gate quietly starts approving label wording because nobody else in the shop will
appearance complaints get answered with thickness numbers that do not address them
verbal reassurance replaces the measured-statement form and leaves no record
acceptance_tests: the charter names the two claims this gate owns, the three referral destinations, and the rule that outgoing statements are measured or estimated-with-method and never promised
revisit_triggers: a sibling gate's scope moves or a new specialist role is added to the shop
a complaint arrives that no gate claims ownership of
the business starts selling into a jurisdiction whose marking rules change who signs claims

base.update_signal: the shop changes what the verification gate may release on its own, or a referral line to appearance, defect diagnosis or compliance is redrawn

nodes.definition: Decide what the piece has to survive before deciding how much gold goes on it. The mechanism is simple and physical: gold is soft, wear removes it, and skin contact plus abrasion plus flexing set the removal rate, so a pendant that hangs, an earring post that sits in a hole, a ring shank that rubs against a neighbouring ring and a bracelet clasp that is grabbed twice a day sit on completely different points of the same curve. The working classes a bench uses are decorative flash (a thin colour layer for display or short-lived fashion goods), light-wear (occasional contact, gentle handling), daily-wear skin-contact, and high-abrasion (shanks, clasps, watch cases). Published wear guidance for these classes exists as handbook-class bands rather than as guarantees - a flash of a fraction of a micrometre is measured in days to weeks of real skin wear, a sub-micrometre deposit carries light wear, and ring and bracelet duty is the multi-micrometre class - and the shop's own logged returns refine those bands for its own chemistry and customers. The class chosen here drives gold cost, plating time, the underlayer decision, which label class the job could ever qualify for, and what may honestly be said about longevity, which is why it is settled at quotation and not at inspection.

included: classing the piece by service duty
translating duty into a thickness specification per zone
expressing wear guidance as handbook-class bands
the cost, time and claim consequences of the chosen class
excluded: the bath parameters that would achieve the thickness
guaranteed wear-life figures
colour or tone selection
approving the marketing word the class would allow

pros.claim: Classing by duty makes the thickness argument concrete and pricable instead of a haggle about 'thicker please'
pros.example: an earring pair for occasional wear and a wedding-band shank in the same order get different specifications and different prices, and the customer can see why

pros.claim: Fixing the class at quotation prevents the far more expensive discovery at inspection that the job was plated for the wrong duty
pros.example: a bracelet clasp quoted and plated to a light-wear class fails its own acceptance criteria at the worst-case zone and has to be stripped and redone at the shop's cost

cons.claim: Duty classing depends on how the customer will really wear the piece, which is self-reported and often optimistic
cons.example: a customer describes a heavy signet as 'special occasions only' and wears it daily, so the deposit reaches base metal far sooner than the class predicted

cons.claim: Heavier classes cost gold and tank time that a fashion-price product cannot carry, so the honest answer is sometimes that the job should not be taken as specified
cons.example: a low-price fashion line cannot economically carry a high-abrasion specification, and the correct outcome is a documented light-wear class with disclosed expectations rather than a quiet compromise

failure_modes: quoting a price against a thin class and then being expected to deliver daily-wear durability
treating a published wear band as a warranty figure
specifying one thickness for a whole piece that has both a hanging face and a rubbing face
acceptance_tests: the job record carries a named wear class, the thickness specification it implies per zone, and the source of that specification (customer duty description plus handbook-class band plus shop history)
the quoted price and cycle time correspond to the specified class rather than to a lighter one
revisit_triggers: a returned piece shows wear-through faster than its class predicted
the customer's description of how the piece is worn turns out to be wrong
the chemistry supplier or a standard revision changes the achievable band for the stack in use

base.update_signal: logged wear-through returns for a product line disagree with the band the class assumed, or a customer's real duty description changes

nodes.definition: Specify and verify the layer beneath the gold, because most of what the customer will experience as 'the gold wore badly' is actually the underlayer failing at its job. An underlayer does three separable things: it levels and brightens so the thin gold above it can look right, it acts as a barrier against base-metal species diffusing up into the gold and dulling or discolouring it over months, and it carries the mechanical load so the soft gold is not being pressed directly into a soft or rough substrate. On copper-bearing bases a barrier layer is doing real chemical work; on steel it is also the corrosion story, because a pore that reaches iron under a noble gold surface creates a cell that drives rust rather than resisting it. The underlayer therefore gets its own written thickness window and its own measurement, usually in the same instrument pass as the gold. Where nickel is the underlayer, skin-contact release is a regulated obligation class of the selling jurisdiction with its own accredited test route, and this gate records the stack and refers that question - it does not answer whether an article is safe for a sensitised wearer, and it never gives medical advice.

included: barrier, leveling and load-carrying roles of the underlayer
a written thickness window for the underlayer
measuring the underlayer alongside the gold
recording the stack so nickel-release obligations can be routed
excluded: choosing or operating the underlayer bath
deciding whether an article is safe for a sensitised wearer
issuing nickel-release results in-house
porosity and corrosion diagnosis, which is referred

pros.claim: Specifying the underlayer converts vague durability complaints into a measurable layer that either met its window or did not
pros.example: a piece that turned dull in three months is checked against the recorded underlayer thickness rather than being blamed on the gold or on the customer's skin

pros.claim: Measuring the underlayer in the same pass costs almost nothing extra and catches a whole class of problems the gold reading hides
pros.example: an XRF pass configured for the stack returns both layers, showing an underlayer at the bottom of its window while the gold looks fine

cons.claim: A thicker barrier layer costs time and can change the feel and fit of a close-tolerance piece
cons.example: a ring already sized to the wearer gains enough stack thickness across a full-duty specification to make a tight fit tighter

cons.claim: Underlayer measurement inherits every limitation of the method used for the gold and adds the ambiguity of a two-layer signal
cons.example: a thin gold layer over a thin underlayer gives an instrument reading in which the two layers and the substrate are hard to separate without a matched calibration

failure_modes: treating the underlayer as an invisible shop detail with no written specification
answering a customer's nickel-sensitivity question from the bench instead of routing it to the regulation class and to professional care
recording only gold thickness so a later diffusion or corrosion argument has no data
acceptance_tests: the job record states the full stack with an underlayer window and a measured underlayer value from a named method
any nickel skin-contact question on the job is recorded as referred to the applicable regulation class and accredited test route rather than answered in-house
revisit_triggers: the substrate family changes for a product line
diffusion-type discolouration appears on returns from a line
the selling jurisdiction's skin-contact release rules are updated or a new market is entered

base.update_signal: a product line shows diffusion-type discolouration on returns, or the jurisdiction's skin-contact release obligations change

nodes.definition: Judge acceptance where the deposit is thinnest and the wear is highest, not where the probe sits most comfortably. Electrodeposition follows the current path, so the outside of a ring, the tip of a prong and the face of a flat pendant plate well while the inside of a shank, the floor of an engraved letter, the shielded area behind a setting and the contact face of a chain link receive far less current and can end up at a fraction of the thickness a proud face reads. Wear works in the opposite direction from the outside in, so the same geometry that plates worst is often the geometry that rubs most. The rule is therefore operational: before the run, the zones are identified on a photograph or sketch of the job and written into the acceptance criteria, and at inspection those zones are the ones that must meet the specification. Proud-face readings still get recorded, because the ratio between proud and recessed readings is a useful running signal about racking and current distribution, but they are never the acceptance number.

included: identifying low-current-density and high-wear zones per job
marking zones before the run
acceptance judged at the marked zones
recording the proud-to-recess ratio as a running signal
excluded: changing racking or current path to fix a thin zone, which is referred to the process specialist
diagnosing why a zone is thin
deciding the thickness number itself

pros.claim: Zone discipline is the single change that stops a shop from shipping pieces that measured fine and wore through anyway
pros.example: the inside of a shank is measured rather than the outside, and a batch that would have passed on outside readings is held

pros.claim: The proud-to-recess ratio becomes a cheap early warning about racking and geometry without any extra instrument
pros.example: a ratio that widens across three consecutive batches of the same product flags a racking or current-path change to the process specialist

cons.claim: Worst-case zones are often exactly the places an instrument cannot easily reach or read
cons.example: the floor of a narrow engraved line is smaller than the measuring spot, so the number has to come from a witness feature or a cross-section instead

cons.claim: Insisting on worst-case acceptance raises the specification the process must actually hit, and therefore the cost
cons.example: meeting the class at a shielded recess means the proud faces receive more gold than they strictly need, which shows up in the gold budget

failure_modes: measuring three convenient points on an outer face and calling it an average
identifying zones after the numbers come back, choosing whichever zone passed
assuming the same zone map applies to a differently-shaped piece in the same order
acceptance_tests: the job record carries a marked zone map made before the run, and every acceptance reading is tied to a named zone on it
at least one recorded reading comes from a low-current-density zone and one from a high-wear zone
revisit_triggers: a new geometry enters a product line
a wear-through return maps to a zone that was never measured
the proud-to-recess ratio shifts materially between batches

base.update_signal: a wear-through return traces to a zone absent from the map, or the proud-to-recess ratio changes materially for a product

nodes.definition: Write down what 'pass' means before the job is plated, because criteria invented after the numbers arrive always pass. The pre-written set is short and specific: the thickness specification per marked zone, the underlayer window, which adhesion methods will be run and what constitutes a pass for each, how many pieces will be measured and from which rack positions, what the shop will do with a borderline result, and who has to be told if the job fails. It is written on the job ticket where the operator will actually see it, not in a policy file. This single habit converts the whole verification gate from an opinion into a test, and it is also what makes a disagreement with a customer survivable, because the standard the job was measured against existed before the result did. Where a criterion cannot be fixed in advance - an unusual substrate, an unknown existing deposit, a piece the customer will not allow to be tested - that uncertainty is written down as a stated limitation rather than quietly resolved later in the shop's favour.

included: per-zone thickness and underlayer criteria written pre-run
named adhesion methods and their pass conditions
sample size and rack spread
borderline-result handling and escalation
written statement of anything that cannot be fixed in advance
excluded: choosing the wear class, which is upstream
running the tests
the disposition decision itself
compliance approval of any claim wording

pros.claim: A pre-written criterion turns a judgement call at inspection into a comparison, which any trained helper can execute the same way
pros.example: a second person running the batch check reaches the same accept-or-hold decision because the pass condition was already on the ticket

pros.claim: It is the artefact that protects the shop in a dispute, because it predates the result
pros.example: a buyer challenging a thickness statement is shown the criteria written at intake alongside the readings taken against them

cons.claim: Pre-writing takes minutes per job and is the first thing dropped when the bench is behind
cons.example: a rush repair goes into the tank with a verbal 'usual spec' and comes out with nothing to measure it against

cons.claim: Criteria fixed too rigidly can be wrong for an unusual piece and then get followed anyway
cons.example: an antique with an unknown existing deposit is measured against a criterion written for new goods, and the total-stack reading is misread as new deposit

failure_modes: writing criteria generically enough that any result satisfies them
recording the criteria somewhere the operator never opens
silently relaxing a criterion once for a deadline and never restoring it
acceptance_tests: the job ticket carries per-zone thickness criteria, the underlayer window, named adhesion methods with pass conditions, sample size and the borderline rule, all dated before the plating run
any criterion that could not be fixed in advance is present as a written limitation with the reason
revisit_triggers: a batch passes its criteria and still generates a complaint
an operator reports that a criterion cannot be executed as written
a new product family enters the shop without a criteria template that fits it

base.update_signal: a job passes its written criteria and still fails in service, or an operator finds a criterion unexecutable at the bench

nodes.definition: Hang sacrificial articles with the work so the tests worth trusting can be run without destroying anything saleable. A witness is a flat coupon or an offcut of the same substrate carrying the same layer stack, racked in the same run and ideally in a comparable position in the current path, so that the bath state, the temperature, the agitation and the current density it saw are the batch's own. Witnesses plated separately, in a different corner of the tank or in a quiet later run, are not evidence about this batch - that is the single most common way a shop convinces itself its adhesion is fine. Witnesses carry the coulometric spots, the bend and wrap, the thermal shock, the cross-section and the thick deposit needed for a meaningful composition reading, and the leftover witness from an accepted batch becomes a retained baseline that any later argument can be compared against. The gold consumed by witnesses is a real recurring cost and belongs in the job's material budget rather than being discovered at the end of the month.

included: same-stack coupons and offcuts racked with the work
position discipline in the current path
assigning destructive tests to witnesses
retaining a witness per accepted batch
budgeting the gold witnesses consume
excluded: destructive testing of customer goods, which requires separate documented consent
racking design itself
what the tests mean, which belongs to each method node

pros.claim: Witnesses make the severe tests affordable, which is what moves a shop from reassurance to evidence
pros.example: a wrap test and a coulometric spot both get run on offcuts while every customer piece leaves untouched

pros.claim: A retained witness per batch turns a future complaint into an investigation with a physical reference
pros.example: a piece returned months later is compared against the witness kept from its own run rather than against memory

cons.claim: A witness only represents the batch if it truly rode with it, and position discipline is easy to lose on a busy rack
cons.example: a coupon clipped to the outer edge of a rack reads thicker than the parts hanging in the middle and creates false confidence

cons.claim: Witnesses consume gold and rack space on every run, which is a real per-batch cost in a low-margin job
cons.example: a small run of light pieces can spend a noticeable share of its gold budget on the coupons that prove it

failure_modes: plating coupons in a separate convenience run and treating them as batch evidence
using a coupon of a different substrate or stack than the goods
consuming the last witness in testing so nothing is retained for the batch record
acceptance_tests: each qualification and production run has at least one witness of the same substrate and stack recorded with its rack position
the destructive results on file name the witness they came from, and one witness per accepted batch is retained and labelled
revisit_triggers: the rack layout or tank changes so that witness position no longer represents the work
a substrate or stack change makes existing coupon stock unrepresentative
witness results and part results diverge repeatedly

base.update_signal: witness results and readings taken from the parts themselves diverge repeatedly, or the rack layout changes the position a witness can occupy

nodes.definition: Use X-ray fluorescence of the ISO 3497 / ASTM B568 class as the non-destructive workhorse for thickness and composition, and know precisely where it stops being trustworthy. The instrument excites the coating, reads the returning characteristic radiation and infers layer thicknesses from it against a calibration - which means the answer is a model fit, not a direct length measurement, and every assumption in that model is a place it can be wrong. Three limits dominate at a jewellery bench. Geometry: the measuring spot must sit inside a flat area, so a thin wire, a narrow shank or a curved bezel smaller than the spot mixes in air and neighbouring angles and degrades the reading unless a small-spot collimator or a flat ride-along witness is used. Depth: a very thin deposit lets the layer beneath dominate the signal, so both thickness and composition readings on a thin flash drift toward the underlayer and under-report the gold. Stack: the calibration must match the actual layer sequence, which is the subject of its own work unit. Within those limits it is fast enough to measure marked zones on finished goods, which is exactly what worst-case acceptance needs.

included: non-destructive thickness and composition of the ISO 3497 / ASTM B568 class
spot-size and curvature handling
thin-coating depth limits
measuring marked zones on finished goods
small-spot collimation and flat witness substitution
excluded: calibration standard management, which is its own unit
destructive confirmation methods
issuing a claimable composition certificate
any adhesion judgement

nodes.definition: Treat calibration as the gate on the instrument rather than an occasional chore, because a wrongly calibrated reading is worse than no reading: it is a confident number that gets written on a job ticket and repeated to a customer. The calibration standards have to represent the actual stack being measured - gold over barrier over the real substrate family - since a standard built for gold on brass encodes different absorption and fluorescence behaviour than gold over nickel over steel, and using the wrong one can shift a thickness result by a large multiple rather than a few percent. The working discipline is: identify the stack, select the matching standard set, verify the instrument against a known foil before the measuring session rather than after it, record that verification in the same log as the readings it authorises, and re-verify after service, transport, a long idle period or any change of stack. Standards themselves age and get scratched, so their condition and identity are part of the record. If no matching standard exists for an unusual stack, that is a stated limitation on every number from that session, not something to be estimated around.

nodes.definition: Use coulometric thickness testing of the ISO 2177 / ASTM B504 class as the shop's affordable destructive anchor, especially where X-ray fluorescence is weakest. A gasketed cell isolates a defined area, dissolves the coating anodically at a controlled current, and the endpoint shows up as a change in cell potential when the layer beneath is reached; the charge that passed converts to a thickness through basic electrochemistry, which makes it a far more direct measurement than a calibrated fluorescence fit. It is strong precisely where XRF is weak - thin deposits, where charge is still charge - and it is usually the first thickness instrument a small shop can justify buying. The costs are real: it leaves a stripped spot, so it lives on witnesses or on hidden areas with documented consent, it needs a different proprietary electrolyte for each coating and substrate pair with the wrong pairing giving a false endpoint, and those electrolytes are hazardous chemicals in their own right. Gold stripping electrolytes are commonly of cyanide- or thiourea-bearing classes, so they inherit the plating room's segregation, labeling, storage, ventilation, PPE and training obligations in full, are never stored or drained anywhere near acids, and are used only per their supplier documentation.

nodes.definition: Decide in advance what happens when two methods give different answers, because they will and the temptation is always to keep the friendlier number. The working ladder has three rungs. First, a routine cross-check: on qualification lots and at a set interval, the same witness gets both a non-destructive reading and a destructive one, and the difference between them is logged as a running instrument-agreement signal rather than resolved case by case. Second, a gross cross-check that needs no instrument at all: the gold consumed by a run, weighed on a fine balance as the difference in part mass or tracked against bath consumption, should be in the same world as the deposited area times the measured thickness, and a mass balance that is badly out points at drag-out, efficiency drift or a measurement error before anyone argues about micrometres. Third, arbitration: where the disagreement exceeds the band the shop has stated, or a buyer disputes a number, a cross-section of the ISO 1463 class settles it by making the layers visible instead of inferred. The rule that makes this work is written before the dispute: the more direct method governs, and the shop investigates the instrument rather than reinterpreting the result.

nodes.definition: Never let a bare number leave the bench. A thickness figure is only meaningful attached to four things: the method class that produced it, the point on the piece it came from, the calibration or electrolyte basis behind it, and the band the shop is willing to stand behind for that method on that geometry. Stated that way, 'measured at the inside of the shank by the non-destructive method against stack-matched standards, within the shop's stated band for that geometry' is defensible; the same figure quoted alone becomes, in the customer's memory, an exact property of the whole piece and a promise. The same rule applies internally, because a number recorded without its method cannot be cross-checked later or used in an arbitration. Where the measurement was constrained - a curved feature, a stack with no matching standard, a piece that could not be witnessed - the constraint is written into the statement rather than trimmed off. This is the discipline that lets the shop be both honest and confident, and it is the direct upstream of every claim and durability statement the business makes.

the internal record form and the customer-facing form
refusing the bare-number form
excluded: mapping a number onto a regulated claim class, which is downstream

nodes.definition: Choose which adhesion methods of the ASTM B571 class actually apply to this job, and write the choice down before the run rather than reaching for whatever is on the bench afterwards. The battery members stress the interface in different ways and are not interchangeable: bending and wrapping puts the coating into tension over a defined radius, a cross-hatch and tape lift attacks a cut edge with a peel force, thermal shock exploits the difference in expansion between coating and substrate, and burnishing works the surface locally. Selection is driven by the goods and by what the piece will endure in life: wire and anything that will be formed after plating demands the bend and wrap because that is the same stress the product will see; flat goods, non-metallic substrates and vapour-deposited surfaces lean on the cross-hatch; stacks whose layers differ strongly in expansion earn the thermal member. Selection is also constrained by what the goods can survive - stone-set, soldered, hollow, enamelled or heat-sensitive pieces exclude the thermal member on the goods themselves, which is one of the main reasons witnesses exist. The output is a named battery with a pass condition per member, recorded on the ticket.

excluding members the goods cannot survive
assigning members to witnesses versus goods

excluded: running the individual tests, which each have their own unit

nodes.definition: Bend or wrap a plated witness over a defined radius and look at what the coating does, which is the most informative adhesion evidence a small shop can generate for free. Wrapping plated wire tightly around a mandrel - with the wire's own diameter as the severest common case - puts the outer fibre of the coating into heavy tension and forces the interface to either hold or let go, and a set of steel rods plus a loupe is the entire apparatus. For a bench that plates wire, chain, bangles or anything that will be formed after plating, this is also the direct experiment that settles the plate-then-form question: if the radius the design requires produces lifting or exposes the layer beneath, the process order has to change so the piece is formed first and plated afterwards. The test is destructive and is therefore a witness and offcut method, run at qualification and repeated on a witness with each production batch. Its result must be read under magnification, because the difference between a coating that cracked and a coating that let go is the difference between an expected characteristic and a rejected batch.

the plate-then-form decision evidence
magnified inspection of the bent zone
excluded: bending customer goods

nodes.definition: Cut a grid through the coating, press a defined pressure-sensitive tape over it and pull, and read what comes away with the tape. This is the quickest adhesion screen and the one most likely to be misused, because it detects only gross failure: a coating with marginal bonding can pass a tape lift comfortably and then peel in service or fail the moment it is bent or thermally shocked. It earns its place in two situations - on flat goods and non-metallic or vapour-coated substrates where bending is impossible and the cut edge is the only practical way to load the interface, and as a fast routine screen between qualifications on a product whose severe results are already on file. Two details decide whether the result means anything: the tape itself is part of the method, so a single named tape is used consistently and a change of brand or age silently changes the test, and the cut has to penetrate cleanly to the substrate without gouging it. The standing rule is that a tape pass is never sufficient evidence for release on its own.

excluded: release on tape evidence alone

nodes.definition: Heat a witness and quench it, and let the mismatch in thermal expansion between coating and substrate try to tear the interface apart. This member of the battery reveals weak bonding that neither tape nor a gentle bend will find, because the stress is generated inside the stack rather than applied from outside, and it typically shows itself as blistering or lifting appearing after the quench rather than during it. The temperature is substrate-dependent and comes from the standard's tabulation for that material class together with the supplier's guidance - it is not a number to invent, and using too high a temperature can change the deposit itself rather than test its adhesion. Two hard boundaries apply. Safety: a hot part going into water produces steam and splash, so this is a controlled operation with proper handling, eye protection and a stable setup, not an improvised toaster-oven stunt. Goods: stone-set, soldered, hollow, enamelled, adhesive-assembled and heat-sensitive pieces must never see this test, because the test can destroy the piece independently of any coating question. That is why it lives on witnesses, and why the selection unit records its exclusion when the goods rule it out.

nodes.definition: Decide what the tested witness is actually showing, because the most expensive mistakes in adhesion testing are made at the loupe rather than at the mandrel. Two very different things look similar at arm's length. Cohesive failure is the coating cracking within itself while remaining bonded: a hard cobalt- or nickel-hardened gold has low ductility and will craze into fine lines at a tight bend radius, and under magnification those lines have no lifted edge, no flaking and no exposure of the layer beneath. That is a characteristic of a hard deposit, not an adhesion reject. Adhesive failure is the coating letting go of what is under it: edges lift, flakes detach, tape carries material away, blisters dome up, and the underlayer or base metal is visible in the failed area. That is a reject and a referral. The call is made under magnification with the evidence photographed into the record, because the same photograph is what settles the later argument about whether the batch should have shipped. When the call is genuinely ambiguous the rule is conservative: treat it as adhesive, hold the batch and refer it, since the cost of holding is a fraction of the cost of a field peel.

photographing the evidence into the record

nodes.definition: Fix, before the run, how many pieces will be measured and which ones, so that the sample is a sample rather than whatever was nearest at the end of the shift. A workable small-shop plan has three parts. A first article: the first piece off the rack is measured fully against the written criteria before the rest of the batch is processed further, which catches a wrong stack or a wrong specification while it is still cheap. A per-batch sample whose size scales with batch size on a rule the shop has written down - a square-root-plus-one style rule is common at bench scale, and shops selling into structured supply chains use an acceptance-sampling class of the ISO 2859 family instead. And a spread rule: the sample deliberately includes pieces from different rack positions, because thickness varies with position in the current path and a sample taken entirely from one corner measures the rack rather than the batch. Alongside this, every piece gets a magnified visual pass, because that costs seconds and catches gross problems the sample would statistically miss. Sampling is a confidence statement, not a guarantee, and the plan says so.

nodes.definition: Separate the heavy proof from the light proof, and be explicit about what forces the heavy one to run again. Qualification is done once per product and process combination: a dedicated lot is plated with witnesses, the full thickness set is measured at every marked zone, the whole selected adhesion battery is run, and the results plus the retained witnesses become the reference the product is judged against afterwards. Routine is what happens on every subsequent batch: first article, the planned sample at the marked zones, one witness through the routine adhesion member, the magnified visual and the record row. The judgement that matters is the list of changes that invalidate a qualification - a new or materially changed substrate or stack, a change of chemistry product or a bath rebuild, a rack or fixture redesign that alters the current path, a different geometry sold under the same product name, a measurement instrument replaced or recalibrated onto different standards, and a long dormancy in which a bath's condition is simply unknown. Shops fail here not by being unable to requalify but by never writing the trigger list down, so the qualification silently ages until a batch fails and nobody can say which change caused it.

the dormancy trigger
